finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation. An unauthenticated caller can make the server request internal hosts, loopback or cloud metadata (for example http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/). The response body is copied back to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF. Error text is also returned.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `target` read at main.go:15 (r.URL.Query().Get("target")) in the /fetch handler
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response body streamed back via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: The /fetch route is registered to the fetch handler
target is taken from the request query string
The response body is reflected to the attacker, which makes this non-blind

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. There is no scheme check, no host allowlist, no resolved-IP check and no auth. http.Get follows redirects by default. Go's http client only speaks http and https, so file:// and gopher:// are not reachable.

verdict.guard_found: none (the allowlist at main.go:27 guards only /safe's safeFetch, not /fetch; no auth middleware)
verdict.reason: main.go:41 routes /fetch to fetch, which takes `target` from the query string at main.go:15, calls http.Get(target) at main.go:16 with no validation, and copies the response body to the caller at main.go:22, so this is full-read SSRF.
